battle.name: 郢州之戰
battle.brief: 至元十一年（1274）秋，丞相伯顏率大軍自襄陽順漢水東下，水陸並行，直取長江樞紐郢州（江夏、鄂州，今武昌）。宋軍據城死守，弩手列城樓；元軍以砲火壓弩陣、雲梯登城，並以舟師封江，援兵不能入。圍城數月而陷，南宋長江防線從此洞開。十字弩為守方重械，亦為攻城方必須壓制的目標。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 郢州之戰是元朝與南宋在江夏（宋稱郢州、鄂州，今湖北武昌）爆發的一場城池攻防戰，交戰時間在元世祖至元十一年（1274）秋冬延至十二年（1275）初。元方由宗王伯顏以征宋丞相之號總領兵馬，兵分三路：伯顏自襄陽率主力沿漢水東下，阿術領兵為之羽翼，阿里海牙另率西路自雲南、廣西方向牽制湖南，使南宋腹背受敵。元軍並非單純的蒙古騎兵，而是蒙古騎兵、契丹兵與漢軍合編的混合兵團，其中漢軍多由歸附的宋地軍人與漢地編成的步軍、水軍構成；水軍由董文炳、董文用一系統率，舟師的規模是元軍攻宋的關鍵，因為漢水與長江恰在郢州匯合，水道同時是進軍通道、糧運線與戰場。宋方則是南宋朝廷直接經營的江防體系：襄樊陷落之後，鄂州、江州一線的守軍多為臨時召集的鄉兵與降而復用的舊軍，指揮中樞雖在丞相賈似道手中，但他封鎖了襄陽失守的消息，朝廷其實並不知道荊襄已亡，軍令與實情嚴重脫節。雙方在兵力性質上形成鮮明對比：元軍是征服者的遠征軍，裝備齊整而水戰生疏；宋軍是守土之軍，熟悉城防與水道，卻士氣低落、上令不統一，一省之防務被分割成許多互不隸屬的小塊。
countriesEn: The Battle of Yingzhou was a siege fought between the Yuan dynasty and the Southern Song at Jiangxia — called Yingzhou or Echangzhou by the Song, present-day Wuchang in Wuhan, Hubei — beginning in the autumn and winter of the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1274) and running into the early months of the next year (1275). On the Yuan side the prince Bayan of the Baarin, acting as chancellor for the campaign against the Song, held overall command, and the army advanced in three columns: Bayan took the main force down the Han River from Xiangyang, Aju commanded the eastern arm, and Aqai (Ali Haiya) led a western column out of Yunnan and Guangxi to pin down Hunan, so that the Song was pressed from two sides at once. The Yuan host was not a purely Mongol cavalry force but a mixed army of Mongol riders, Khitan and Han troops, the Han element being recruited from the surrendered populations of the Song and organised as infantry and naval units; the fleet under Dong Wenbing and the other Dong-family commanders was the decisive part of it, because the Han and the Yangtze meet at Yingzhou, and the waterway was at once the avenue of advance, the supply line and the battlefield. On the Song side stood the river defence system run directly by the Southern Song court. After the fall of Xiangyang and Fancheng, the garrisons of Echangzhou and Jiangzhou consisted largely of hastily summoned militia and old troops taken back into service; the centre of command lay with Chancellor Jia Sidao, though he sealed off the news of the fall of Xiangyang, so that the court did not know that Jingxiang was already lost and the orders of the day bore no relation to the actual situation. The contrast between the two armies was stark: the Yuan force was an invading expedition, well equipped but green on the water; the Song force defended its own soil, knew its walls and its river intimately, yet was hollowed out by low morale and divided command, with the defence of a single province split into many mutually independent fragments.
people: 伯顏（1236—1295），蒙古巴林部宗王，與忽必烈同族而年長數歲，1271年任中書右丞相，1274年受命總領征宋兵事，攻下郢州後乘勝追至建康、臨安，1276年奉詔班師，1290年進錄尚書令，1295年病卒於大都。他是此役事實上的統帥，戰役的方針由他定下：速取江漢樞紐，再順流直下江淮。阿術（1227—1285），畏兀兒出身的元將，長於水戰，自襄陽追宋舟師至鄂州，與伯顏合兵破郢州，1275年冬率舟師入臨安，追奔宋室於海岱。阿里海牙，元初西域宿將，領西路軍取雲南、廣西，1275至1276年間攻下潭州、靜江、邕州，與中路伯顏形成鉗形攻勢。董文炳與其兄弟董文用等董氏將領，統率漢軍水師，董文炳受命督造戰船、徵集役夫，率舟師自黃河、淮入漢水，保障漢水航線的糧運並控制水面。張弘範（1238—1280），西漢軍統制張柔之子，自襄樊之役便在軍中，郢州城破時為先登之卒，後統兵追亡宋至崖山。宋方：丞相賈似道（1238—1285）以主和為名專擅軍權，屯兵江陵、鄂州一帶而不援襄陽，襄陽失守後又封鎖消息；郢州守將高達力戰拒守，文天祥曾為他作《高制干》一詩紀其守江之功，相傳城破被擒後不屈而死；襄樊降將呂文煥受伯顏差遣，移檄江淮諸州縣勸降，瓦解了沿江抵抗的士氣。
peopleEn: Bayan of the Baarin (1236–1295) was a Mongol prince of the same lineage as Kublai Khan and several years his senior; he became Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat in 1271 and in 1274 was ordered to take overall command of the war against the Song. After the reduction of Yingzhou he pursued the Song to Jiankang and Lin'an, was ordered to withdraw the army in 1276, and was advanced to Grand Chancellor in 1290; he died at Dadu in 1295. He was the effective commander of this campaign, and the plan of the operation was his: strike fast at the hinge of the Han and the Yangtze, then drive straight down the river toward Jianghuai. Aju (1227–1285), an Uyghur-born Yuan general skilled in river warfare, chased the Song fleet from Xiangyang to Echangzhou, joined Bayan in taking Yingzhou, and in the winter of 1275 led his ships into Lin'an in pursuit of the Song court. Aqai (Ali Haiya), a seasoned commander from the western regions, took the western column through Yunnan and Guangxi and reduced Tanzhou, Jingjiang and Yongzhou between 1275 and 1276, forming a pincer with Bayan's advance from the centre. Dong Wenbing, together with his brother Dong Wenyong and the rest of the Dong family, commanded the Han navy: Dong Wenbing was charged with building war boats and levying labour, and his fleet came down the Yellow and Huai rivers into the Han, securing the grain route and control of the water for the Yuan. Zhang Hongfan (1238–1280), son of the Han commander Zhang Rou, had been in the field since the Xiangyang campaign and was among the first over the wall at Yingzhou; he later led the pursuit of the Song remnant to Yamen. On the Song side, Chancellor Jia Sidao (1238–1285) monopolised military power behind a policy of peace, sitting on his troops around Jiangling and Echangzhou instead of relieving Xiangyang and sealing off the news of the disaster; the defender of Yingzhou was Gao Da, for whom Wen Tianxiang wrote the poem 'Gao Zhi Gan' in memory of his defence of the river, and who fought to the end, tradition holding that he was captured, refused to yield and died in captivity; Lü Wenhuan, the Song commander who had surrendered at Xiangyang, was used by Bayan to issue proclamations urging the river prefectures and counties to submit, which dissolved the morale of the Song resistance along the water.
kits: 十字弩即本卡兵器，是這場攻防中守軍最重要的遠程兵器，攻守雙方都圍著它做文章。弩以弩機絞弦上弦，張力遠強於手弓，箭矢粗重、破甲能力高，卻把射速交給了機械：裝填要分兩步，先以絞繩或牛角弩機張弦，再由人工掛矢，臨陣射速遠遜於弓手。宋軍把弩配置在城樓、雉堞與馬面之上，居高臨下俯射城外接近道路，成為守城的主幹火力；弩位之外以步弓補射近處與填補射界，弓弩混用，彌補弩的裝填空檔。蒙古攻城部隊則以砲火壓制城頭弩陣：襄樊之役已大量使用的回回砲（配重式投石機）與火藥兵器，能在射程外打散城頭射手，再以雲梯、穴地（地道）、填壕等手段讓步卒貼近。弩手在城頭的優勢是居高與固定射界，弱點是裝填慢、難以轉移；一旦城頭被砲火或登城部隊擾動，弩陣就會出現火力空隙，這正是元軍選攻城而非曠野會戰的理由之一。除十字弩外，雙方還用到：蒙古騎兵（按千戶、萬戶編制，配長刀、標槍與弓箭，以速度與衝擊見長）、漢軍步卒（扛旗、守械、填壕、扛雲梯）、大型水軍舟師（董文炳部所督，戰船以數千艘計，載兵載糧、衝撞封鎖江面），以及各類攻城器械與障礙器材；宋軍一側則備有投石機、猛火油一類燃燒性守城器材、擂木、滾木、拒馬與鹿角，另有沉船與鐵索橫江，阻擋元軍戰船順流而下。糧秣方面，漢水與長江是唯一的大宗運輸線，元軍由襄陽轉輸荊州、鄂州一線，宋軍靠江州、江西與湖廣的漕運接濟，兩條線的順逆，在郢州一役中直接決定了誰能撐得更久。
kitsEn: The crossbow of the card is the most important missile weapon of the defenders in this siege, and both sides built their tactics around it. The crossbow is cocked by a mechanism, a winch or a horn-and-lever lock, giving far more power than a hand bow and a heavy bolt able to pierce armour; but the machine takes over the rate of fire, and loading takes two stages — the string must first be drawn back by the mechanism, and only then can a soldier hook a bolt into the groove, so the practical rate of fire is far below that of a bowman. The Song army mounted crossbows on the towers, the battlements and the horse-face walls, shooting down from above onto the approaches: that was the backbone of the defence. Beyond the crossbow slots they used ordinary bows to cover the short range and fill the gaps left by the slow reload, mixing bow and crossbow to make up for the lost rate of fire. The Mongol siege troops answered with artillery fire meant to suppress the crossbow line on the wall: the counterweight trebuchets already used in great numbers against Xiangyang, together with gunpowder weapons, could break up the wall-top shooters from beyond their own range, after which ladders, mining and filling of the ditch allowed infantry to close. The crossbowman's strength on the wall is his height and his fixed field of fire; his weakness is the slow reload and the difficulty of shifting position. Once the wall was shaken by artillery or by men who had already reached it, the crossbow line opened gaps, which is exactly why the Yuan army chose to assault rather than to meet the Song in the open field. Besides the crossbow, both sides used Mongol cavalry organised in thousands and ten thousands, with sabre, lance and bow, winning by speed and shock; Han infantry, who carried banners, manned siege engines, filled ditches and bore scaling ladders; the great river fleet under Dong Wenbing, several thousand war boats carrying troops and grain and used to ram and seal the river; and a full range of siege engines and obstructions. The Song side had its own trebuchets, incendiary materials such as burning oil, dropped stones and rolling logs, chevaux-de-frise and antler-shaped barriers, and also sunken boats and iron chains stretched across the river to stop Yuan war-craft coming down with the current. For supply, the Han and the Yangtze were the only bulk transport arteries: the Yuan moved grain from Xiangyang through Jingzhou to the Echangzhou line, while the Song drew on the grain traffic of Jiangzhou, Jiangxi and Huguang, and which way those two lines ran decided, in this campaign, who could hold out longer.
tactics: 元軍的戰法是典型的水陸合擊加攻城。主力自襄陽順流而下，舟師佔據江面，兩岸由蒙古騎兵與漢軍步卒護行，先以舟師封鎖漢水與長江在郢州匯合處的水道，切斷城中對外的水路交通，再用砲兵在城外展開，對城頭弩手與城樓實施壓制，步卒則以雲梯、穴地與填壕接近城牆，趁城頭火力空隙登城。攻城與封江互相配合，使宋軍最擅長的長江水路反過來成了困局：援軍縱然在江州、九江一帶集結，戰船也過不來，因為河道已被元軍舟師與沉船、鐵索之類的障礙控制。江面爭奪是此役的關鍵，傳聞元軍曾派死士夜入江中排除障礙、解去鐵索，隨即以舟師突入江心。守城一方把宋廷倚重的長弓與弩做成分層射擊：城頭弩負責遠程重擊，雉堞下的步弓與弓箭手補射城根下的攻城器械，滾木與擂木壓制貼城的雲梯。守軍也曾趁夜出城焚燒元軍攻城器械與營壘，但整體指揮受制於文官掣肘、援軍逗留，出城反擊多為一陣即退。城外各縣邑在元軍移檄與前線戰敗消息的雙重作用下陸續歸降，郢州遂成孤城。城破之後，守軍或隨伯顏受降被編入漢軍，繼續沿江作戰，或散入湖廣山區，成為此後數年地方武裝的一部分。
tacticsEn: The Yuan method was typical of this war: a combined assault by land and water, followed by a siege. The main body came down the river from Xiangyang with the fleet holding the middle of the channel and Mongol cavalry and Han infantry escorting along both banks. The fleet first sealed the waterway where the Han meets the Yangtze at Yingzhou, cutting the city off from waterborne contact with the outside, and then the artillery deployed in front of the walls to bear on the crossbowmen and the towers, while infantry closed with ladders, mining and filled ditches and went up whenever the wall-top fire slackened. Siege and blockade reinforced one another, and the very river that the Song had relied on now worked against it: even if relief armies gathered at Jiangzhou and Jiujiang, their boats could not get through, because the channel was in the hands of the Yuan fleet and of sunken craft and iron chains. The struggle for the river was the crux of the battle; it is said that the Yuan sent men into the channel by night to clear the obstructions and cut the chains, and then drove the fleet into the middle of the river. The defenders, for their part, laid their crossbows and bows in layers: the wall-top crossbows for heavy shooting at range, ordinary bows and archers at the foot of the battlements to cover the siege engines working against the base of the wall, and dropped stones and rolling logs to crush the ladders brought close to the wall. The garrison also made night sorties to burn the Yuan siege engines and camps, but the overall command was hamstrung by civilian officials vetoing the generals and by relief armies that never came, so a sortie seldom lasted beyond a single charge. With the Yuan proclamations and the news of defeat working together, the counties around the city surrendered one after another, and Yingzhou was left isolated. After the walls fell, some of the defenders surrendered and were enrolled in the Han army to fight on along the river; others scattered into the mountains of Huguang and became part of the local armed resistance of the following years.
data: 時間線最為清晰：至元十一年（1274）夏，元廷下詔全面攻宋，伯顏總兵；同年七月前後大軍離開襄陽，順漢水東行約三百公里的航道，九月前後兵鋒抵達郢州城下，圍攻延續數月，至十二年（1275）初城池陷落。若以襄陽至臨安計，全程約一千五百公里的漢水與長江水道，元軍自1274年秋出發到1276年二月臨安出降，前後不足兩年。兵力方面，伯顏所統大軍與隨征漢軍合計當在數萬之眾，同期文書與後世記載常以「十萬」或「數十萬」稱之，顯係誇大之辭，實際作戰兵力遠少於此；董文炳所督水軍戰船以數千艘計，是當時世界上規模最大的內河舟師之一。宋方守軍則難以確切統計，江州、鄂州、黃州一線的沿江汛軍加上郢州守軍，多有臨時徵集的鄉兵，總數同樣以數萬計，但分散作戰、缺乏統一指揮，士氣亦低。攻城階段的傷亡數字各書互相矛盾，常見的說法是元軍死傷以數千計、宋軍被俘與潰散者亦以萬計，這類數字皆無可靠底冊，僅可作為量級參考。距離與航路上，襄陽至郢州沿江約三百公里，郢州再順流至江州約二百五十公里，航道在郢州是漢水轉入長江的轉折點，這一點決定了此役的戰略價值。武器消耗方面，弩的裝填速率明顯低於弓手，可射出的箭矢數只及弓手的一小部分，因此攻城期內弩箭的儲備量與備用弩機的數量，直接決定城頭能持續壓制的時間。
dataEn: The chronology is the clearest part of the record. In the summer of the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1274) the Yuan court issued the general order for the conquest of the Song and gave Bayan supreme command; around the seventh month the army left Xiangyang, worked its way down the roughly three hundred kilometres of navigable Han, and by about the ninth month the vanguard stood beneath the walls of Yingzhou. The siege ran for several months and the city fell in the early months of the following year (1275). Measured from Xiangyang to Lin'an, the whole route was some fifteen hundred kilometres of the Han and the Yangtze, and the Yuan went from leaving Xiangyang in the autumn of 1274 to the surrender of Lin'an in February 1276 in less than two years. On numbers of men, Bayan's army together with the Han troops taken into Yuan service was certainly in the tens of thousands; contemporary documents and later accounts habitually speak of a hundred thousand or several hundred thousand, which is plainly rhetorical, and the real fighting strength was far smaller. Dong Wenbing's fleet numbered several thousand war boats and was among the largest inland fleets in the world at the time. The Song garrison cannot be counted with any precision: the river garrisons of Jiangzhou, Echangzhou and Huangzhou together with the troops of Yingzhou were largely hastily summoned militia, and the total was again in the tens of thousands, but scattered, without unified command and in poor spirits. Casualty figures for the siege contradict one another from source to source; the usual claims, that the Yuan lost several thousand men and that tens of thousands of Song soldiers were taken or scattered, rest on no reliable roll and can only be taken as an order of magnitude. On distances and routes, the run from Xiangyang to Yingzhou is about three hundred kilometres by the river and about two hundred and fifty more from Yingzhou down to Jiangzhou, and it is precisely at Yingzhou that the Han turns into the Yangtze — a fact that gives the battle its strategic value. On the consumption of weapons, a crossbow reloads far more slowly than a bow and can put only a fraction of the arrows into the air, so the stock of bolts and the number of spare locks held in the city decided how long the wall-top fire could be kept up.
cause: 這場戰爭的第一層起因是襄樊的失守。蒙古自1267年起經營襄陽、樊城，以回回砲與水陸封鎖攻打了六年，至1273年樊城先破、襄陽隨降，荊襄屏障崩潰，南宋的長江防線從此再沒有任何縱深可以退守。第二層起因是元廷的戰略決策：至元十一年，忽必烈正式下詔全面滅宋，命伯顏總領兵馬，兵分三路，準備由襄漢順流而下，先取江夏、郢州，控住漢水與長江的交會點，再直取建康、臨安。這個方案並非臨時起意，襄樊降將劉整早已獻策，強調循漢水東下、取荊襄而斷江淮樞紐；劉整於同年病故，未及親見郢州之役，但其遺策在伯顏手中落地。配合西路，阿里海牙自雲南、廣西方向攻取潭州與靜江，使南宋無法專注江漢，形成兩面鉗擊。第三層起因在宋廷內部：丞相賈似道以主和為名專擅軍權，把襄陽失守的消息封鎖了數月，朝廷直到蒙古大軍順流東下才如夢初醒；他不肯以全軍出援而屢次遷延，坐失戰機。南宋朝廷另有自身的難處：連年戰費與加派使財政吃緊，邊軍欠餉與軍籍混雜削弱了戰鬥力，士氣被內部政治消耗殆盡。於是在蒙古軍兵臨城下時，宋廷既無可信的情報，也無可用的應變機制，只剩下城牆與運氣。
causeEn: The first layer of cause was the fall of Xiangyang and Fancheng. The Mongols had been at work against Xiangyang and Fancheng since 1267, besieging them for six years with counterweight trebuchets and a blockade of the water by land and river; in 1273 Fancheng fell first and Xiangyang followed, the barrier of Jingxiang collapsed, and the Southern Song's line along the Yangtze was left with no depth at all to fall back on. The second layer was the strategic decision of the Yuan court: in the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1274) Kublai Khan issued the general order for the destruction of the Song, gave Bayan supreme command, and split the army into three columns to advance down the river from Jingxiang, seize Jiangxia and Yingzhou first, hold the meeting point of the Han and the Yangtze, and then strike straight at Jiankang and Lin'an. The plan was not improvised: Liu Zheng, the Song general who had surrendered at Xiangyang, had long counselled advancing along the Han and cutting the hinge of Jianghuai by taking Jingxiang; Liu Zheng died of illness in the same year and never saw the battle of Yingzhou, but his strategy was carried out under Bayan. In concert, Aqai came out of Yunnan and Guangxi against Tanzhou and Jingjiang so that the Song could not concentrate on the Han region, producing a pincer from two directions. The third layer of cause lay inside the Song court: Chancellor Jia Sidao monopolised military power behind a policy of peace and sealed off the news of the fall of Xiangyang for several months, so the court learned of the facts only when the Mongol army was already coming down the river; he would not commit the whole army to the relief and deferred again and again, losing the opportunity. The Song had its own troubles as well: years of war costs and surtaxes had emptied the treasury, unpaid and irregularly registered troops had sapped the fighting force, and morale had been consumed from within by the politics of the capital. So when the Yuan army stood before the city, the Song had neither trustworthy intelligence nor a workable means of response, and nothing remained but the walls and luck.
impact: 郢州陷落的直接後果，是元軍在長江中游取得了一個完整的據點與一座現成的舟師基地。從此江防線被從中央戳破：元軍可以在郢州就地徵糧、造船、囤兵，不必再從襄陽長途轉輸；宋軍則被切斷在江漢與江淮之間，兩岸州縣失去統一指揮。次年的戰局因此急轉直下：1275年元軍在丁家洲與宋軍水師主力決戰，宋軍舟師全軍覆沒，沿海防線崩潰；同年元軍進軍建康、平江；1276年二月臨安出降，宋恭帝北去，南宋朝廷覆亡；其後宋室流亡海上，1279年在崖山被元軍水師追上，宋室覆滅。郢州因此成為元滅宋最後一場關鍵城池攻防的起點，歷史書寫常把它與襄樊之戰並列，一守一攻，同屬長江樞紐之爭。對湖南、江西而言，阿里海牙西路與伯顏東路的合擊使州縣多不戰而降，郡縣守令各自為政，民間則湧起義軍，文天祥即於1275年在江西起兵組織義軍，試圖以地方武裝延續抗元。在制度層面，元朝在江南以招撫與減賦為主要手段接管，伯顏班師後受封賞，其部將亦分封江南；蒙古貴族由草原征服者轉為江南新興的土地貴族，江南的財政與人力從此持續供應北方都城，奠定了元一統的物質基礎。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the fall of Yingzhou was that the Yuan obtained in the middle Yangtze a complete base and a ready-made naval yard. The river line had been pierced at its centre: the Yuan could levy grain, build boats and quarter troops on the spot instead of hauling everything the long way from Xiangyang, while the Song was cut off between the Han region and Jianghuai, and the prefectures on both banks lost any central direction. The course of the war then turned sharply: in 1275 the Yuan met the main body of the Song fleet at Dingjiazhou and destroyed it, collapsing the coastal defence; in the same year the Yuan advanced into Jiankang and Pingjiang; in February 1276 Lin'an surrendered and the Song emperor was taken north, ending the Southern Song court; the remnants of the house then fled to sea and were overtaken by the Yuan fleet at Yamen in 1279, and the Song was extinguished. Yingzhou is therefore the opening move of the last decisive siege of the Yuan conquest, and historians commonly set it beside the siege of Xiangyang: one a defence, one an assault, both fought for the hinge of the Yangtze. For Hunan and Jiangxi, the combination of Aqai's western column and Bayan's advance from the centre brought the surrender of prefectures without a battle; the local officials governed for themselves, and armed bands rose in the countryside, Wen Tianxiang raising a force in Jiangxi in 1275 to continue the resistance through local warfare. At the institutional level, the Yuan took over the south with pacification and reduced taxes as its principal methods; Bayan was rewarded on his return and his officers were enfeoffed in the south, and the Mongol nobility turned from steppe conquerors into a new landholding aristocracy of the south. The wealth and manpower of Jiangnan thenceforth supplied the northern capital without interruption, providing the material base of the Yuan unification.
result: 結果是元軍攻下郢州，宋方守軍潰散，城市落入元軍控制。此役之後，元廷在江夏置軍政機構，設總管府鎮守，以郢州（江夏、鄂州、武昌）為江南西部的樞紐，漢水與長江兩條水道自此長期置於元軍控制之下，宋人再無力北望襄鄂。伯顏乘勝追擊：鄱陽湖、廬山、饒州一線的宋軍在江面潰散後，元軍舟師直抵江州、饒州，至元十二年（1275）冬取建康，次年二月臨安出降，滅宋大局至此奠定。郢州守軍的結局則是多向的：一部隨城投降，被元軍收編為漢軍，繼續沿江作戰；一部由江道散入湖廣山區，成為此後數年地方武裝的一部分；守將高達的去向，諸史說法不一，或謂被擒不屈而死，或謂脫身而去，說法本身即說明當時江防崩潰之倉促。從兵器史的角度看，此役是弩與砲在同一座城牆上對抗的樣本：弩給了宋軍數月的縱深，砲與雲梯最終越過了弩，決定了城牆的歸屬；宋廷可以靠弩守住一座城，卻不能靠弩守住一個王朝的航道。
resultEn: The outcome was that the Yuan took Yingzhou, the Song garrison was scattered, and the city passed under Yuan control. After the campaign the Yuan court set up military and civil administration at Jiangxia with a headquarters to garrison it, making Yingzhou — Jiangxia, Echangzhou, Wuchang — the hinge of the Yuan west of the Yangtze; the Han and the Yangtze remained in Yuan hands for the rest of the dynasty, and the Song could never again look north towards Jing and E. Bayan pursued the beaten enemy: after the Song forces were scattered on the water around Poyang Lake, Lushan and Raozhou, the Yuan fleet drove straight for Jiangzhou and Raozhou, took Jiankang in the winter of the twelfth year of the Zhiyuan era (1275), and in February of the next year Lin'an surrendered, settling the fate of the Song. The defenders of Yingzhou, for their part, went to several ends: some surrendered with the city and were taken into the Han army to fight on along the river; some dispersed by the waterways into the mountains of Huguang and became part of the local armed groups of the years that followed. The fate of the commander Gao Da is given differently from source to source — some accounts have him dying unyielding in captivity, others have him escaping — and the disagreement itself shows how suddenly the river defence collapsed. From the point of view of the history of arms, this campaign is a specimen of the crossbow and the artillery in opposition on one and the same wall: the crossbow gave the Song a few months of depth, but the artillery and the ladders finally got past the crossbow and decided who owned the wall. The Song court could hold a city with crossbows; it could not hold the navigation of a dynasty with them.
